title: Micro-change catalogue: heuristics, rollback triggers, and test probes
content:
Context and intent:
- Quick personal catalogue for tiny surface changes (sub-5-line edits, dependency pin bumps, tiny config flips).
- Goal: reduce cognitive overhead when deciding whether to land quickly, who to add as reviewer, what probes to run, and exact rollback steps.
- Keep this lightweight: the aim is <10 min pre-merge checks most of the time.

Heuristic checklist (fast pass, positive = OK to land with single reviewer):
1) Scope sanity: change touches only one logical concern (codepath, config flag, single test). If more than one, escalate.
2) Test footprint: unit tests cover added lines or unchanged behaviour. If no tests added but existing tests exercise change, mark as manual smoke required.
3) Dependency risk: if bumping dep minor/patch + changelog shows no breaking API, ok. Major semver -> require release-engineering signoff.
4) Hot path: does change run on token-generation hot path (serving runtime inner loop)? If yes, require perf quickbench (see probes).
5) Migration/DB: any schema/format changes -> block until migration plan exists.

Recommended reviewers by surface area (fast mapping):
- Serving runtime: Marcus Li or eng-serving-runtime oncall
- Console/rollouts: Elena Torres or product-hosted-api eng lead
- Observability/metrics: Put SRE alias + include perf diffs

Pre-merge quick probes (aim < 10 minutes):
- Unit + smoke: run unit suite for changed package; run 1-2 quick integration smoke jobs (local docker-ish).
- Static checks: run lint, typecheck, safety-audit (deps).
- Perf probe for hotpath: run microbench (local harness) with 1000 short sequences, compare mean latency vs baseline; if >5% regression, block.
- Canary config: if toggled flag, add rollout config entry with 0.1% initial weight and a canary monitor.

Rollback and mitigation playbook (copyable):
- Immediate revert (fast): revert commit -> push -> prod automated pipeline (if commit is small).
- Quick feature flip: if change behind feature flag, flip flag to safe default and monitor.
- Hotfix branch: if revert unsafe, cherry-pick fix to hotfix branch and deploy.
- Postmortem seeds: timeline + basic impact metrics (error rate, p50/p95 latency, token throughput), initial root-cause hypothesis.

Post-merge followups (1 day / 3 day / 1 week):
- Day 1: confirm canary metrics return to baseline; if anomaly, escalate to oncall.
- Day 3: add small integration e2e that covers edge case introduced by change (if not present).
- Week 1: verify any telemetry flags and update dashboards if needed.

Snippets / copy-paste PR description template (tiny changes):
- Summary: one-line description of change and reason.
- Scope: list of files touched and logical boundary.
- Tests: what ran locally + CI (unit/smoke).
- Rollout: feature flag (yes/no), canary plan if applicable.
- Rollback: revert commit or flip flag.
- Reviewers: @<primary>, @sre-oncall if observability touched.

Quick examples (notes to self):
- Bumped numpy 1.23.5 -> 1.23.7 for security patch: quick checks: run unit tests, run inference microbench, confirm no ABI extras. Outcome: landed with single reviewer (non-hotpath).
- Small tweak to batcher lock ordering (serving runtime): required perf probe, caught 7% p95 regression, reverted and reworked approach.

Open questions / friction points to iterate on:
- Can we automate the microbench for hotpath checks as a presubmit job with a short history baseline? Today it requires manual baseline setup.
- Better one-click canary creation for micro-changes (console UX).
- Standardize minimal PR template per team (reduce free-text).

Short todo (actionable):
- [ ] Add this template to personal snippets and team README.
- [ ] File small infra ticket: presubmit microbench harness (INF-920).
- [ ] Add brief howto in Confluence (link above) for rollback steps.

Random brain dump (for future refinement):
- Low-risk merge lanes: docs-only, comment tweaks, tests-only, minor deps with patched vendors.
- Medium-risk: config toggles that touch rollout paths, small logic changes in non-hotpath code.
- High-risk: anything touching KV cache, attention cache, or runtime scheduling.

End notes:
- Keep conservative on hotpath changes; it's cheaper to iterate in branch + perf bench than to coordinate rollbacks under load.
- This is a living note; prune monthly after seeing what habits actually help.
